scope: Local read-only independent flash-plan audit. No SSH, no runtime changes, no script edits, no secret or credential file access. Deployment itself remains with the root agent.

hook_audit.required_change: If kernel8 entry content changes, e.g. release logger text, calculate its final SHA after staging and extend/update the exact allow-list. Never keep a stale single hash and assume firmware collectors will run. Keeping both reviewed old/new entry hashes preserves downgrade behavior.
hook_audit.preserve_fallback: If no trusted integrated entry is present, execute /jffs/ledg-node-fix/ensure.sh and /jffs/node-web-fix/apply.sh exactly as before; stock slot2 uses that path.
hook_audit.deployment_gate: Back up current hook and compare against the recorded hash before replacing. If live content differs, inspect the delta rather than blindly overwriting.

hook_audit.required_change: None solely because the kernel changes. Existing logic already recognizes /usr/libexec/ledg-node/rc by exact patched SHA. Change the allow-list only if a separately reviewed executable really changes; keep model, role, stock rc and payload checks.
None if it continues calling the same reviewed RGB ensure hook. Preserve existing contents and execute mode.

No kernel-number gate exists. It accepts each existing web file only when its SHA is stock or the reviewed patched SHA. Integrated UI assets must retain those exact hashes unless intentionally updated with matching manifest. Fallback path starts JFFS collectors.

Their hardware/role guards depend on stock /sbin/rc SHA, not kernel version. Preserve that executable. Preserve integrated CCR configuration path /jffs/ccr-status/curl.conf and disable-file semantics; no credential belongs in the image.

packaging_gates.gate: Integrate the existing UI/RGB/collectors before packaging
packaging_gates.detail: At audit time build/candidate-rootfs-v8 and rootfs-v8.zstd.squashfs are kernel/modules plus stock userspace only (0 non-module differences); they are not replacements for the kernel6-ui1 integrated rootfs. Copy the reviewed non-module integration and rebuilt kernel8 modules, then verify a deliberate change manifest.

packaging_gates.gate: Test exact integrated rootfs/kernel/modules in QEMU
packaging_gates.detail: Do not substitute the bare kernel8 rootfs or only the previous UI image. Record final kernel, bootfs, rootfs and package SHA/lengths plus asset hashes and startup entry SHA.

pack-image.py verifies the known original FIT SHA and old PSS signature, replaces only inner kernel, signs/verifies new header, asserts all non-kernel boot payloads identical and no loader update. Preserve those checks; use the final integrated rootfs as the actual rootfs payload, not a stale build/rootfs.zstd.squashfs.
bootfs payload <50MiB and rootfs payload <200MiB. Assert model GT-BE19000AI, exact package SHA, bootfs/rootfs extracted lengths and hashes.

CONFIG_GTBE19000AI_TRIAL_METADATA_RO=y is present in configs/kernel8.config. Run existing trial-guard.cpio.gz with Image-v8 and complete QEMU-only arguments loop.max_part=8 be19000ai_trial_disk=loop0; marker QEMU_TRIAL_GUARD_COMPLETE. Never include the disk override on hardware.
packaging_gates.initial_setup_failure: The first kernel8 guard invocation omitted loop.max_part=8; blockdev --rereadpt failed and init exited before guard assertions. Kernel6 successful command had this argument. This is a fixture setup failure, not evidence of a kernel metadata-guard regression.

deployment_sequence.action: Capture fresh state before any mutation
checks: productid GT-BE19000AI
uname, boot_id and /proc/cmdline
bcm_bootstate active, next, committed, both commit flags
/dev/{metadata,bootfs,rootfs} symlink mapping and partition sizes
full stock slot2 hashes
current JFFS hook hashes and sufficient RAM/JFFS free space
Current metadata1/metadata2 (256KiB each), GPT/partition map and boot-state text
Private current JFFS tree and NVRAM settings backup with restricted permissions; never print/include credentials
Original bootfs2/rootfs2 verified by full hashes; preserve existing known-good backups
Current trial bootfs1/rootfs1 if retaining a rollback to kernel6-ui1 is desired; original slot2 remains mandatory fallback
Keep backups out of Git/package; private data remains private

deployment_sequence.action: If active slot is still trial1, reboot back to the already selected stock2
checks: Require recorded next boot=Second and slot2 committed before reboot
No metadata unlock or boot-state mutation is needed for the normal trial1→stock2 reboot
Wait for new boot_id; require root=/dev/mmcblk0p6, Booted Partition Second and slot2 commit1
Verify full stock2 hashes and management/network return; stop if state differs
Never flash slot1 while it is active; never let inactive-slot selection target committed slot2

deployment_sequence.action: Stage final package and exact-hash persistent hook changes while on stock2
checks: Upload under an explicit unique .pkgtb basename, never /tmp/linux.trx (historic flasher live-update branch)
Verify remote package hash equals final local package hash
Verify bcm_flasher SHA c029cd3d59a42d23c0bc4508eb8f04b82781c0eb097644f57e5de075c53f570d
Validate updated hooks with sh -n, ownership/executable mode, atomic replacement and previous-hash precondition
Retain original JFFS fallback assets and do not change AiMesh role, hostname, SL1680 or credentials

deployment_sequence.action: Use a new kernel8-specific guarded flash wrapper from stock2
checks: Derive all package/payload hashes and exact lengths from the final manifest; rc1-flash.sh values are obsolete
Require active Second/root p6, committed2, first commit0, second commit1 and expected next Second
Write inactive slot1 only through the reviewed bcm_flasher path; capture return status/log and sync
Hash exact-length prefixes of bootfs1/rootfs1 and compare with extracted payload hashes
Hash entire bootfs2/rootfs2 again and require unchanged originals
Require first commit0/second commit1 and next Second after write; do not arm a failed readback

deployment_sequence.action: Arm exactly one boot of slot1 only after successful readback
checks: Existing utility syntax: bcm_bootstate 6 (BOOT_SET_PART1_IMAGE_ONCE)
Read back Booted Second, Reboot First, slot1 commit0, slot2 commit1
Back up resulting boot-state/metadata evidence, sync, capture previous boot_id and reboot once
Do not use +1, permanent PART1 state5, or any uncommit of slot2

deployment_sequence.action: Validate physical kernel8 trial before accepting it
checks: New boot_id plus uname #8 and root=/dev/mmcblk0p4; watcher SSH reconnect alone is insufficient
Live /proc/config.gz hash matches configs/kernel8.config
Booted First, slot1 commit0, slot2 commit1, next boot Second
mmcblk0p1/ro and p2/ro both1; expected trial guard messages in dmesg
Check PSI system and cgroup statistics/monitor availability with bounded read-only probes
Verify three radios, BE98 controller AiMesh state/wired backhaul, Ethernet/Runner, AI internal link
Verify exact integrated web assets, no unintended /www bind overlays, RGB process executable, firmware collectors, fresh panel telemetry
Record unexpected diagnostics separately from the previously observed Serdes warning; no blanket warning-free claim
Leave slot1 uncommitted; preserve automatic next-reset fallback to original2

automatic_commit_guard.mechanism: Partition policies are set read-only before metadata1/metadata2 are published, blocking vendor rc metadata writes during trial boot.
automatic_commit_guard.not_a_security_boundary: An operator can explicitly clear BLKROSET or write the raw disk; do neither during this deployment.
automatic_commit_guard.recovery_semantics: One-time selection reverts the following boot choice to committed slot2. It does not by itself guarantee a hung kernel triggers a timely reset; a reset is still needed for fallback to execute.

watcher_limitations: watch-trial.py --version only chooses evidence file names; it does not assert uname/config/rootfs match kernel8.
It stops after first newly booted authenticated SSH session, which could be original fallback; inspect returned boot identity.
Timeout writes observations but is not an acceptance failure exit code; deployment needs an explicit success/failure gate.
AI SSH-open is only port reachability, not container/service or internal-link health.

deployment_state_relayed_by_root.source: Root agent deployment observation; this audit did not SSH
